label: IBM India
headline: Named the most influential Technical Experts Council member in India

year_layers.narrative: Joined IBM India Software Labs in July, straight from engineering college, building JAX-WS web-services support for IBM's Lightweight Infrastructure.
Became component owner for the Lotus Expeditor toolkit, led an internship project that earned a Bravo award, and started organizing the lab's hackdays.
Co-authored three IBM developerWorks articles and organized five innovation events, from Hackday 7 to the first Lotus Knows, earning two Bravo awards.

Led IBM India's Hackday 8 and won its best-implementation prize, was named the most influential Technical Experts Council member in India, filed my first US patent and became worldwide lead for the Lotus Expeditor Webcontainer.

Promoted to staff engineer on an industrial condition-monitoring solution; recognized by the lab's VP, in the regional general manager's report and with an Eminence and Excellence award; co-led IBM University Relations' T2E challenge.
numbers: 3 invention disclosures and 5 abstracts from team IP sessions

year_layers.narrative: An IBM Master Inventor and my first manager wrote public recommendations; my patent application was published and a second disclosure went out on IP.com.

quote.text: He had, in a very early stage of his career started getting involved in the project initiatives, mentoring interns and other technical vitality activities, which showed his leadership capabilities.

year_layers.narrative: Left IBM in March after five years and nine months; the availability patent was granted and has since been cited 27 times.

arc.what: Joined IBM India Software Labs, Bengaluru, as Associate Software Engineer on JAX-WS web services for Lightweight Infrastructure 8.1.x.
Developer and component owner for the Lotus Expeditor toolkit and runtime.
Promoted to Software Engineer and made worldwide lead for the Lotus Expeditor Webcontainer.
Promoted to Staff Software Engineer, Natural Resources Center of Excellence (condition monitoring).
Left IBM after five years and nine months to lead development at Exeter.

signatures.title: Worldwide owner of an IBM product component
signatures.body: Delivered two Lotus Expeditor toolkit releases with defects brought to near zero, then led the Webcontainer worldwide, solved two critical severity 1 customer defects and took open severity 1 and 2 defects to zero.

signatures.title: From first disclosure to a granted US patent
signatures.body: My availability invention was approved for filing in 2010, earned IBM's CEO-signed invention award, and was granted as US 8,560,487, since cited by 27 patents; later I ran invention-mining sessions that gave my team 3 more disclosures.

signatures.title: Building the lab's technical community
signatures.body: Organized Hackdays 6 to 8 and advised 9 and X, won Hackday 8's best-implementation prize, and was named the most influential Technical Experts Council member in India.

quotes.text: He had, in a very early stage of his career started getting involved in the project initiatives, mentoring interns and other technical vitality activities, which showed his leadership capabilities.
He has been responsible for driving the org level Hackday event with Universities in South, which is also a very popular program within IBM Software Labs in India.

company.took: IBM is where I learned to build. I owned a component that customers depended on worldwide, filed my first patent, and ran hackdays across India that turned ideas into working software. I learned that the work around the job, the events, talks and inventions, compounds as much as the job itself. I still believe the fastest way to grow is to own something end to end and invite others in.
